newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat condition continues improvement.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat condition continues improvement.

text.p: Condition ratings for Kansas winter wheat improved for the second consecutive week, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop report.

The crop was rated eight percent excellent, 47 percent good, 34 percent fair, nine percent poor and two percent very poor. The previous week 14 percent had been rated poor or very poor and two weeks ago the total was 22 percent.
The report said statewide 87 percent of the crop was jointing up from an average of 86 percent. Five percent had headed, as of Sunday, down from an average of 13 percent.
Wheat streak mosaic and leaf rust had been reported in some areas while there were also reports of alfalfa weevil and aphids in some fields.

Warmer temperatures allowed farmers to resume spring planting. Corn was 50 percent planted, slightly behind the five-year average of 55 percent. Grain sorghum and soybean planting had just begun, the report said.

Topsoil moisture was rated eight percent surplus, 81 percent adequate and 11 percent short. Pasture condition was rated six percent excellent, 62 percent good, 27 percent fair, four percent poor and one percent very poor.
